newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean union body demands 10.6 pct wage hike.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean union body demands 10.6 pct wage hike.

text.p: South Korea's outlawed union body on Tuesday demanded an average of 10.6 percent wage increase this year for its members, a spokesman for the body said.

"We are asking for a 10.6 percent wage increase," said Yoon Young-mo, spokesman for the 500,000-strong Korean Confederation of Trade Unions. "We'll fight for the raise and continue our call to revoke the current labour law."

The confederation spearheaded almost a month of strikes after parliament, last December, in a clandestine session with no opposition lawmakers present, rammed a controversial labour law which underminded job stability.
On Monday a watered-down version of the legislation, endorsed by both ruling and opposition parties, was passed by the National Assembly.
